arxiv-2105-11220.title: Towards Parallel CFD computation for the ADAPT framework
arxiv-2105-11220.creator: Imad Kissami † ∗ {}^{\dagger}{}^{\ast}, Christophe Cerin †, Fayssal Benkhaldoun ∗, Gilles Scarella ∗
arxiv-2105-11220.description: Abstract In order to run Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) codes on large scale infrastructures, parallel computing has to be used because of the computational intensive nature of the problems. In this paper we investigate the ADAPT platform where we couple flow Partial Differential Equations and a Poisson equation. This leads to a linear system which we solve using direct methods.

arxiv-2107-05436.title: First-order phase transformation at constant volume: a continuous transition? Journal: Eur. J. Phys.
arxiv-2107-05436.creator: V. F. Correa & F. J. Castro
arxiv-2107-05436.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by V. F. Correa & F. J. Castro. We describe a first-order phase transition of a simple system in a process where the volume is kept constant. We show that, unlike what happens when the pressure is constant, (i) the transformation extends over a finite temperature (and pressure) range, (ii) each and every extensive potential (internal energy U U , enthalpy H H , Helmholtz energy F F and Gibbs energy G G ), and the entropy S S , is continuous across the transition,

arxiv-2202-02817.title: Beas : Blockchain Enabled Asynchronous & Secure Federated Machine Learning
arxiv-2202-02817.creator: Arup Mondal, Harpreet Virk, Debayan Gupta
arxiv-2202-02817.description: Abstract Federated Learning (FL) enables multiple parties to distributively train a ML model without revealing their private datasets. However, it assumes trust in the centralized aggregator which stores and aggregates model updates. This makes it prone to gradient tampering and privacy leakage by a malicious aggregator.

arxiv-2211-04802.title: Future ALICE upgrades for Run 4 and Beyond
arxiv-2211-04802.creator: H. Sebastian Scheid
arxiv-2211-04802.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by H. Sebastian Scheid. ALICE pursues several upgrades to further extend its physics reach. For Run 4, ALICE is pioneering the construction of truly cylindrical tracking layers, which will improve the measurements of heavy-flavour hadrons and dielectrons. In addition, a Forward Calorimeter (FoCal) for the measurement of direct photons is being developed to access the gluon distributions of nucleons and nuclei at low x x . For Run 5 and beyond, ALICE 3 is proposed.

arxiv-2211-10326.title: Vanishing adsorption admissibility criterion for contact discontinuities in the polymer model
arxiv-2211-10326.creator: Yulia Petrova, Bradley J. Plohr, Dan Marchesin
arxiv-2211-10326.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Yulia Petrova, Bradley J. Plohr, Dan Marchesin. We introduce the vanishing adsorption criterion for contact discontinuities and apply it to the Glimm-Isaacson model of chemical flooding of a petroleum reservoir. We prove that this criterion, which derives from a physical effect, justifies the admissibility criteria adopted previously by Keyfitz-Kranzer, Isaacson-Temple, and de Souza-Marchesin for models such that the fractional flow function depends monotonically on chemical concentration.

arxiv-2305-04264.title: ATLASGAL: 3-mm class I methanol masers in high-mass star formation regions Preprint: W. Yang,
arxiv-2305-04264.creator: W. Yang, Y. Gong, K. M. Menten, J. S. Urquhart, C. Henkel, F. Wyrowski, T. Csengeri, S. P. Ellingsen, A. R. Bemis, J. Jang
arxiv-2305-04264.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by W. Yang, Y. Gong, K. M. Menten, J. S. Urquhart, C. Henkel, F. Wyrowski, T. Csengeri, S. P. Ellingsen, A. R. Bemis, J. Jang. Class I methanol masers are known to be associated with shocked outflow regions around massive protostars, indicating a possible link between the maser properties and those of their host clumps.

arxiv-2312-14584.title: Asymptotics of Distances Between Sample Covariance Matrices
arxiv-2312-14584.creator: Roberto Pereira, Xavier Mestre, and David Gregoratti
arxiv-2312-14584.description: Abstract This work considers the asymptotic behavior of the distance between two sample covariance matrices (SCM). A general result is provided for a class of functionals that can be expressed as sums of traces of functions that are separately applied to each covariance matrix.

arxiv-2401-15391.title: MultiHop-RAG: Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Multi-Hop Queries
arxiv-2401-15391.creator: Yixuan Tang, Yi Yang
arxiv-2401-15391.description: Abstract Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) augments large language models (LLM) by retrieving relevant knowledge, showing promising potential in mitigating LLM hallucinations and enhancing response quality, thereby facilitating the great adoption of LLMs in practice. However, we find that existing RAG systems are inadequate in answering multi-hop queries, which require retrieving and reasoning over multiple pieces of supporting evidence.

arxiv-2410-10732.title: Efficient Simulation of Open Quantum Systems on NISQ Trapped-Ion Hardware
arxiv-2410-10732.creator: Colin Burdine, Nora Bauer, George Siopsis, Enrique P. Blair
arxiv-2410-10732.description: Abstract Simulating open quantum systems, which interact with external environments, presents significant challenges on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices due to limited qubit resources and noise. In this paper, we propose an efficient framework for simulating open quantum systems on NISQ hardware by leveraging a time-perturbative Kraus operator representation of the system’s dynamics.

arxiv-2508-21015.title: Investigating the Performance of Adaptive Optics on Different Bases of Spatial Modes in Turbulent Channels
arxiv-2508-21015.creator: Rojan Abolhassani, Lukas Scarfe, Francesco Di Colandrea, Alessio D’Errico, Khabat Heshami, Ebrahim Karimi
arxiv-2508-21015.description: Abstract Quantum key distribution (QKD) allows secure key exchange based on the principles of quantum mechanics, with higher-dimensional photonic states offering enhanced channel capacity and resilience to noise. Free-space QKD is crucial for global networks where fibres are impractical, but atmospheric turbulence introduces severe states’ distortions, particularly for spatial modes.

pmc-11545663.creator: Marco Carilli, Valerio Iacovelli, Marta Signoretti, Antonio Luigi Pastore, Franco Gaboardi, Giovannalberto Pini, Mario Falsaperla, Roberto Falabella, Pierluigi Bove
pmc-11545663.description: Simple SummaryUreteral stricture disease is a rare but fearsome complication after radiation therapy for pelvic malignancies. Several minimally-invasive managements have been proposed: however, the optimal strategy is still a matter of debate, and available literature on this topic is rather heterogeneous.

pmc-11690448.title: GRIEF COACH, A TEXT-BASED GRIEF SUPPORT INTERVENTION: ACCEPTABILITY AMONG HOSPICE FAMILY MEMBERS
pmc-11690448.creator: Emma Payne, Melissa Lunardini
pmc-11690448.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Although older adults experience more bereavement, they are less likely to seek support. This poses significant risks, including increased risk for prolonged grief disorder, mood disorders, loneliness, and other adverse health outcomes (Ghesquiere, 2013). Limited service access and uptake among older populations can be attributed to factors such as inadequate Medicare coverage, shortage of trained providers, and a dearth of bereavement care options tailored to the unique preferences and needs of older adults (Bartels, 2003).

pmc-12426013.title: Smarce1 fine-tunes cardiomyocyte proliferation in the embryonic zebrafish heart
pmc-12426013.creator: Deung-Dae Park, Tillman Dahme, Leonie Krieg, Steffen Just, Wolfgang Rottbauer
pmc-12426013.description: IntroductionThe molecular mechanisms regulating cardiomyocyte (CM) proliferation during heart development are essential for understanding regenerative processes but remain incompletely defined. While adult mammalian CMs are post-mitotic, zebrafish retain proliferative capacity throughout life. We aimed to identify genetic regulators that fine-tune CM proliferation during cardiac development.

pmc-12647850.title: Crossover interference mediates multiscale patterning along meiotic chromosomes
pmc-12647850.creator: Martin A White, Beth Weiner, Lingluo Chu, Gyubum Lim, Mara Prentiss, Nancy Kleckner
pmc-12647850.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Meiotic crossover interference is a one-dimensional spatial patterning process that produces evenly-spaced crossovers. Quantitative analysis of diagnostic molecules along budding yeast chromosomes reveals that this process sets up two interdigitated patterns, of shorter and longer periodicity, by “two-tiered” patterning. Both tiers comprise clustered assemblies of three types of molecules (“triads”) representing the three major components of meiotic chromosomes (crossover recombination, axes, and the synaptonemal complex). One tier of triads occurs at sites of majority (“canonical”) crossovers.

pmc-12705208.title: Pouvons-nous encore sauver la traumatologie au Canada?
pmc-12705208.creator: Edward J. Harvey, Chad G. Ball
pmc-12705208.description: lité, sur la recherche relative aux résultats des traumatismes, sur les soins après une blessure (dépendances, santé mentale et réadaptation), sur le récidivisme chez la patientèle ou sur le bien-être des chirurgiens et chirurgiennes, le constat est clair : une crise secoue notre système national de soins en traumatologie.

pmc-13053980.title: Protocol for pro-inflammatory microRNA motif discovery using machine learning
pmc-13053980.creator: Chien-Yu Lin, Boyang Ren, Shiming Yang, Rosemary Kozar, Lin Zou, Brittney Williams, Wei Chao, Peter Hu
pmc-13053980.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummaryHere, we present a protocol to identify nucleotide motifs that predict the pro-inflammatory property of microRNAs (miRNAs) using machine learning. We describe steps for cell culture, miRNA transfection, pro-inflammatory classification, and k-mer discovery. We detail procedures for combining in vitro macrophage assays with exhaustive motif searches and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression to define nucleotide sequence features that distinguish pro-inflammatory miRNAs.

pmc-13564101.title: Optimization of Microstructured Silicon Attenuated Total Reflectance Fourier Transform Infrared Elements
pmc-13564101.creator: Eleanor L. Osborne, Aneesh Vincent Veluthandath, Waseem Ahmed, Ganapathy Senthil Murugan
pmc-13564101.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Microstructured silicon attenuated total reflection (ATR) Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) elements, commonly known as microstructured silicon reflection elements (μSREs), are gaining popularity as a low-cost, disposable alternative to ATR crystals in fields such as medical diagnostics. They comprise a silicon chip, with light incident on microprisms on the underside guided into the chip and totally internally reflecting at the sample interface.

pmc-13602140.title: Anti-proliferative and anti-inflammatory potential of 2-chloro-3-((4-hydroxyphenyl)amino)naphthalene-1,4-dione through targeting TNF-α/IL-8 and NF-κB signaling in HCT116 cancer cells: a comprehensive in silico docking and in vitro study
pmc-13602140.creator: Sakdiphong Punpai, Panupong Mahalapbutr, Panyakorn Taweechat, Ronnakorn Leechaisit, Kiattawee Choowongkomon, Ratchanok Pingaew, Wanlaya Tanechpongtamb
pmc-13602140.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Colorectal cancer (CRC) is closely associated with chronic inflammation, and the NF-κB pathway acts as a central regulator of the inflammatory response that promotes tumor progression. In this study, we examined the anticancer and anti-inflammatory potential of anilino-1,4-naphthoquinone derivatives (compounds 3, 8, and 12) in CRC models using in vitro assays, in silico analysis with the Gold program, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. HCT116 cells were pre-exposed to these compounds before LPS stimulation. Cytotoxicity was determined using the MTT assay.

pmc-13605026.title: Parental Competencies as Familial Protective Factors in Adolescent Substance Use Prevention: A Scoping Review
pmc-13605026.creator: Kyung-Young Hong, Jihye Shin
pmc-13605026.description: Highlights What are the main findings? Thirty-two publications identified 11 parental competency domains relevant to adolescent substance use prevention.Relational bonding, prevention communication, monitoring, and rule-setting were the most frequently represented competencies.Parental competencies were more often targeted in interventions than directly measured or examined in relation to adolescent substance-use outcomes. What are the implications of the main findings?
